title: Contrix Cursor
description:
Single opaque cursor type. Used as both stream continuation token (incremental sync, list pagination — 'since', 'after_cursor', 'prev_cursor', 'next_cursor') and barrier token (read-your-writes wait — 'X-Contrix-Wait-For'). The wire form is always cx:cursor:<base64url(canonical_json)>. Clients MUST treat the wire form as opaque; only the issuing server reads the inner structure. The 'purpose' field discriminates how the cursor is consumed.

Integrity contract (normative, see client-sync.md §12 and encoding.md §10): every cursor MUST be server-verifiable in one of two forms — (A) stateless self-describing cursor with mandatory '_mac' or '_sig' covering the canonical body (transcript binds purpose, principal_id, device_id, service_id, filter_hash, positions, target?, x, issuer_kid); or (B) stateful opaque-handle cursor whose body is reduced to {v, purpose, h, x} where 'h' is an unguessable server-side handle that the issuing server resolves to the bound (principal, device, service, filter_hash, purpose, positions, expiry) tuple. Servers MUST validate integrity (verify MAC/signature, or look up handle) before using the cursor to advance to-device acknowledgement, /sync since position, X-Contrix-Wait-For barrier, or 'dropped'/'resync_required' recovery state. Integrity failures map to 'cursor_integrity_invalid' (distinct from 'cursor_expired' which is a TTL outcome).

purpose.description: Cursor purpose. 'stream' = continuation cursor for incremental sync / list pagination. Used as 'since' on /sync, 'before' / 'after' on cx.events.query (including its service-to-service federation pull form GET /api/v1/events?before=<cursor>), and as response 'prev_cursor' (older direction) / 'next_cursor' (newer direction). prev_cursor / next_cursor carry absolute directional meaning regardless of how the request was issued — see api-conventions.md §7.0. 'barrier' = read-your-writes / wait-for-event cursor (use in X-Contrix-Wait-For header to block until local frontier covers target.event_id). 'stream' cursors MAY include 's' (Realm frontiers) and 'd' (device positions). 'barrier' cursors MUST include 'target'.

s.description: Per-Realm frontier (stream cursors). Key is realm_id; value pins the frontier this cursor describes for that Realm.

target.description: Required when purpose='barrier'. Identifies the specific event whose causal frontier the consumer must reach before answering.

x.description: Expiration timestamp (Unix ms). MUST be in the future when the cursor is issued. TTL upper bounds (cursor lifetime = x - t_ms): barrier cursors MUST have TTL ≤ 3,600,000 ms (1 hour); stream cursors MUST have TTL ≤ 604,800,000 ms (7 days). Issuing a cursor exceeding these caps is a producer error; receivers MUST reject with `invalid_param`. Reasoning: barrier cursors only gate read-your-writes wait latency and become meaningless once the global frontier has long covered the target event. Stream cursors lose causal alignment value over weeks of activity.

h.description: Server-side opaque handle (stateful cursor form). When present, the cursor body MUST be reduced to {v, purpose, t, x, h} — the 's', 'd', 'target' state fields MUST be absent and instead resolved by the issuing server from the handle. The handle MUST be unguessable (≥ 128 bits entropy after base64url decoding). minLength=22 enforces that floor mechanically: base64url packs 6 bits per character so 128/6 ≈ 21.33 → at least 22 chars of the [A-Za-z0-9_-] alphabet are required to encode 128 bits. The handle MUST be bound by the issuing server to (principal_id, device_id, service_id, filter_hash, purpose, positions, target?, expiry), and revocable. Servers MUST reject any unknown / expired / cross-binding handle with `cursor_integrity_invalid`. This is the integrity path for implementations that do not want to embed a MAC/signature; it is the moral equivalent of Matrix `next_batch` / MSC4186 `pos` and satisfies the integrity contract without crypto. A cursor that contains 'h' MUST NOT also contain '_mac' or '_sig' (handle lookup is itself the integrity check); a cursor without 'h' MUST carry '_mac' or '_sig'.

_mac.description: HMAC over the cursor's canonical bytes (every property EXCEPT `_mac` itself, encoded per RFC 8785 JCS). Wire form: `hmac-<alg>:<hex>`; alg MUST be hmac-sha256 or stronger (hmac-sha384 / hmac-sha512). The hex MUST be 64 / 96 / 128 lowercase hex chars matching the alg's tag length. Transcript MUST bind purpose, principal_id, device_id, service_id, filter_hash, positions, target?, x, issuer_kid (see encoding.md §8.3.1). MUST appear iff the cursor is in stateless form (no `h`). MUST NOT appear together with `h` or `_sig`.

_sig.description: Detached JWS signature over the cursor's canonical bytes (every property EXCEPT `_sig` itself, encoded per RFC 8785 JCS). Format is compact JWS `<protected>.<payload?>.<signature>` (base64url segments separated by dots). Same transcript binding rules as `_mac`. MUST appear iff the cursor is in stateless form (no `h`). MUST NOT appear together with `h` or `_mac`.

allOf.description: Integrity contract: either 'h' (stateful handle) MUST be present, or '_mac' / '_sig' (stateless self-describing). Handle form and MAC/sig form are mutually exclusive — handle lookup is itself the integrity check.

^_(?!mac$|sig$)[A-Za-z0-9_]*$.description: Server-private auxiliary fields (e.g. `_compress` / `_kid` flags). Names MUST start with underscore and MUST NOT be `_mac` or `_sig` (those are typed top-level properties with explicit constraints — see `_mac` / `_sig` above). Auxiliary `_*` fields are excluded from cursor migration translation but MUST be included in `_mac` / `_sig` canonical transcript so they cannot be silently stripped or injected. Implementations MUST NOT use `_mac_foo` / `_sig_bar` / similar to spoof integrity fields — only the exact names `_mac` and `_sig` are integrity-bearing, and this pattern explicitly excludes them so the typed property constraints govern.
